description: Run Actions page (dev-only) — a detailed log of every GUI automation action executed during a workflow run. Shows clicks, keystrokes, scrolls, and other low-level actions with their status, coordinates, and screenshots.

groups.name: Action Log Viewing
groups.description: Developers use this page to inspect the full sequence of GUI actions that were executed during an automation run. Every click, type, scroll, and hover is recorded and displayed in a table format. The user needs to quickly scan the action list to understand the automation flow, identify where things went right or wrong, and correlate actions with the visual state of the target application at each point.

assertions.description: The user can see a table or list of all GUI actions that were executed during the run, with each action showing its type (click, type, scroll, etc.), status (success/failure), and timestamp, providing a complete audit trail of automation activity

The user can click on any action row to view detailed information about that specific action, including screenshots, coordinates, and full execution context, enabling deep debugging of individual automation steps
The user can see the total number of actions executed, giving them a quick sense of the automation complexity and helping identify unexpectedly short or long action sequences

groups.name: Action Failure Debugging
groups.description: When GUI automation actions fail (element not found, click missed, unexpected dialog), developers need to quickly identify which action failed and why. The action log should make failures visually prominent and provide enough context to diagnose the root cause without switching to other tools. This is the primary debugging workflow for visual automation issues.

assertions.description: Failed actions are visually distinct from successful ones (through color coding, icons, or other visual indicators), allowing the user to immediately spot failures in a long action sequence without reading every entry
When an action has failed, the user can access the error message or reason for failure, providing diagnostic information about why the automation step did not complete as expected

The user can view screenshots associated with actions (particularly failed ones), showing exactly what the screen looked like when the action was attempted, which is essential for diagnosing visual automation mismatches

groups.name: Empty State Handling
groups.description: Not all workflow runs produce GUI actions. Runs that are purely AI-driven (command and prompt workflows) will have no action log entries. The page should clearly communicate this to the developer so they do not mistake an empty log for a bug. The empty state should be informative and suggest that the run may not have included GUI automation steps.

assertions.description: When no GUI actions were recorded for the selected run, the user sees a clear empty state message explaining that no actions exist, preventing confusion about whether data failed to load or simply does not exist
While action log data is being fetched, the user sees a loading indicator confirming that the system is retrieving data, distinguishing the loading state from the empty state
